newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher for second day.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher for second day.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended higher Friday, for the second day in a row, after gold, silver and platinum greeted the new year with sharp falls earlier this week.

"But the outlook for gold and silver is ultimately still bearish, with gold likely to fall further longer term to around $340 an ounce and silver may see $4.40 an ounce," Smith Barney Washington DC-based analyst Phil Tiger said.
"The fundamentals have not changed and supply and demand data for gold and silver are difficult to estimate with accuracy anyway," he said.
COMEX February gold closed up $1.40 an ounce at $360.20, after rallying to $360.60, testing Tuesday's intraday high.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $358.80/30, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $358.25, and the New York close Thursday at $357.80/359.20.

"Fund shortcovering, the OTC options expiry in London today, some overnight Japanese buying after the further slump in the Tokyo stock market, the strong US December jobs data and the rise in US bond yields on the threat of inflation, were all factors behind today's gains in precious metals," Refco New York analyst Tim Porter said.

Open interest in February gold futures fell 2,288 lots to 100,613 contracts Thursday, in data released Friday, suggesting some short covering by funds may be occurring, analysts said. In recent weeks, fund net short open interest in gold futures has been near record levels.

Spot gold lost more than $13.00 an ounce or about 3.5 percent in the first few days of the new year, posting new three year lows at $355.00, on fund selling, producer hedging and concern about European central bank sales.
But in a radio report Friday, the central bank of France Friday denied it had been selling its gold reserves, joining the Bank of Portugal which issued a denial earlier this week.

The sharp fall in the gold price in recent weeks will likely hurt gold mining companies fourth quarter 1996 earnings and earnings for the first quarter 1997, with high cost producer's now only marginally profitable, analysts said.

Toronto-based TVX Gold Inc said earlier this week it would close its Casa Berardi mine near Quebec, while in December Vancouver-based Placer Dome Inc said it would also close two small mines near Quebec and stop work at its high-cost Paymaster mine in northern Ontario.
But Australian producers may be less affected because of their tendency to hedge more of their forward earnings, analysts said.
The Philadelphia Stock Exchanges's index of North American gold and silver miners .XAU fell to 13 month low this week at 106.94, before closing Friday at 113.01.
Meanwhile, COMEX is to narrow the strike price increments for gold options for the first three months from Monday.
Increments for strike prices below $500 an ounce in the nearby three exercise months will become $5.00 an ounce.
"The change will probably lead to even higher options volumes and open interest," Smith Barney options analyst Carmen Knoepffler said.
Gold remains the weakest component of the precious metals complex, with the spot gold/silver ratio falling further to 75.53 by the close Friday, from down from 77.53 on January 2.
COMEX March silver ended up 3.0 cents an ounce at $4.765, after seeing a five day high at $4.7850 intraday.

Open interest in March silver rose 1,060 lots to 62,424 lots Thursday, suggesting funds were re-establishing long positions, after some liquidation of the small fund net long position was seen in the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders report last Monday.
Gold also remain weaker than platinum with the April platinum/gold spread widening to $7.00 an ounce Friday, from $5.40 Thursday.
NYMEX April platinum closed up $2.30 at $369.00, with NYMEX March palladium ending down five cents at $125.95.
